cards.front: Recall a key point about Customer Service
cards.back: Good customer service creates competitive advantage: it builds loyalty, generates repeat business, and encourages positive word-of-mouth recommendations (free marketing).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Customer Service
cards.back: Methods of delivering customer service: well-trained staff, clear returns policies, efficient complaint handling, after-sales support (warranties, helplines), personalised communication, and multichannel support (phone, email, chat, social media).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Customer Service
cards.back: Monitoring customer service: customer feedback surveys, mystery shoppers, complaint analysis, online reviews, and Net Promoter Score (NPS).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Customer Service
cards.back: Handling complaints effectively: listen, acknowledge, resolve quickly, and learn from the complaint to prevent recurrence. A well-handled complaint can increase customer loyalty.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Customer Service
cards.back: Poor customer service costs businesses: lost sales, negative reviews, damaged reputation, and higher marketing costs to replace lost customers (acquiring a new customer costs 5-7 times more than retaining one).

cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating customer service investments, use the RACE framework: Retention (how many customers stay?), Acquisition (does service attract new customers through referrals?), Cost (what does poor service cost in complaints and lost sales?), Efficiency (does good service reduce complaints and returns?). Good customer service is an investment, not a cost.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Handling customer complaints well means always giving the customer what they want, even if it's unreasonable. Correct: Good complaint handling means resolving the issue fairly and professionally, not simply giving in to every demand. AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Customer Service with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

cards.front: Understanding Customer Service in Business Context
cards.back: Customer Service is a key topic in GCSE Business Studies that affects how businesses operate in the UK economy. Understanding this concept requires knowledge of both theoretical principles and real-world application. The AQA specification requires you to explain, analyse and evaluate business concepts using appropriate terminology, and apply them to real business scenarios using UK examples.

cards.front: Applying Customer Service to UK Business Examples
cards.back: For customer service, applying theory to practice means using real UK business examples to illustrate your understanding. Small businesses face different challenges from large corporations when dealing with customer service. Consider how factors like business size, ownership structure, industry sector and market position affect the impact of customer service on a business.

cards.front: Exam Technique for Customer Service Questions
cards.back: GCSE Business exam questions about customer service range from 1-mark definition questions to 12-mark evaluation questions. For definition questions (1-2 marks), give a precise business definition. For explanation questions (3-4 marks), define and explain with a brief example.
